rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still aligned). PGS000753 is best supported because it provides the clearest PRS-comparable signal via an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) alongside a disease-focused publication context (AAA genetic architecture in MVP) and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), whereas most others primarily report full-model discrimination or weakly comparable metrics. Runners-up: PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) with only basic covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex), but lacks PRS-only metrics so the apparent performance may be covariate-driven; PGS003972 similarly reports only full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates; PGS001784 (global biobank framework) provides a PRS-comparable Nagelkerke R2 (covariates regressed out) of 0.014661 but is penalized by framework-style study archetype despite large validation; PGS002054 (UKB portability framework) has a similar PRS-comparable partial-r (0.0144) but likewise framework-penalized and lacks clearer PRS-only discrimination. Confidence is moderate because key candidates rely on non-PRS-only full-model metrics (PGS003973/PGS003972) and the two PRS-comparable R2/partial-r candidates come from framework/portability studies, leaving some unresolved comparability across the pool. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (alcohol dependence) via trait_efo/phenotyping alignment: PGS002738 and PGS002739 explicitly map to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder"; PGS000201/PGS000202 map to trait_efo="alcohol dependence measurement" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder (DSM-5 criteria count, log-transformed)", which is closely aligned but slightly more measurement/quantitative. PGS002738 is best supported because it has the most directly aligned trait_efo plus the strongest visible discriminative evidence (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a reasonably sized EUR evaluation (n=7,900) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS). Remaining limitations: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUC/R2; covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739, reducing comparability, and the pool mixes EUR-only vs AFR-only evaluation (PGS002739), so the best choice depends on intended deployment ancestry (not provided). Runners-up: PGS000201 next due to aligned AUD DSM-5 endpoint and higher incremental ΔR² (0.01192) than PGS000202 with similar PRS-CS and EUR eval; PGS002739 follows due to direct AUD/alcohol dependence mapping and supportive OR (1.76) but AFR-only evaluation and gene-based small variant set (858); PGS000202 last due to weaker ΔR² (0.00456) and smaller validation n (1,251).

All 3 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis; phenotyping_reported is an alcohol-related cirrhosis endpoint in each). PGS000704 is best supported structurally: it uses a genome-wide snpnet multi-PRS approach with very large variant count (183,271) and reports time-to-event discrimination (C-index/full-model 0.711) with only basic covariates (age as time scale, sex, batch, PCs), plus an HR per SD of 1.18 (modest but non-null signal). However, the evidence is limited because the reported discrimination is full-model (not PGS-only), so it cannot be cleanly compared as standalone PRS performance.

Runners-up: PGS004913 is disease-focused and endpoint-aligned with basic covariates and provides a PRS-comparable R² (0.029) plus an OR top-vs-bottom deciles (4.4), but it is based on a small SNP set (20) and modest training size (n=3,037). PGS001777 is also endpoint-aligned and reports strong stratification (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18), but it is extremely sparse (3 variants), has unknown covariates, and has a small validation sample (n=1,390) with a lower full-model AUROC (0.671). Overall, no candidate provides clearly comparable PGS-only AUROC/R² across the set, keeping confidence below High. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 19 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported explicitly angina/I20/PheCode 411.3). Among them, PGS001262 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity (doctor-diagnosed angina), reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.58683; PGS-only R2=0.01304) plus incremental AUROC (0.0098), and uses only basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs) with a reasonably sized European validation (n=49,472). The main limitation is that PGS001262 comes from a pan-trait sparse-PRS framework publication (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable externally than disease-focused scores; however, within the visible direct-match set, several newer alternatives (e.g., Commun Biol 2024 models PGS004457/PGS004527) lack comparable PRS-only metrics and have unknown covariates, and the MVP 2024 benchmarking models (PGS0050xx) report only full-model C-index/OR without clear PRS-only discrimination, making them harder to rank above a model with explicit PGS-only performance. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS001261 and PGS001260 are near-identical framework siblings with slightly weaker PGS-only metrics than PGS001262; PGS005048 and PGS005052 have strong reported effect sizes (OR≈1.49 per SD) and good full-model C-index (~0.766) on an angina phecode endpoint, but lack explicit PRS-only metrics and have N/A training-size metadata, lowering comparability confidence. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 9 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align to ankylosing spondylitis), so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS002089 is preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a large variant set (22,026) and reports a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0919, EUR validation), which is more informative than full-model AUROC alone and structurally stronger than sparse/low-variant framework scores. Main limitation: several candidates come from framework/benchmarking contexts (including PGS002089 from a UKB portability study), and many alternatives lack PRS-only AUROC/R²; the Taiwanese EAS models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates, making their discrimination less comparable. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS001267 and PGS001268 have explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² and basic covariates but are very sparse (10 variants) and from a pan-trait sparse framework; PGS003420 has the highest reported AUROC among the EAS disease-focused set but only as full-model AUROC with unknown covariates; PGS001876 is another UKB portability score with fewer variants and lower partial-r than PGS002089. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it has exact trait alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis; phenotyping_reported = incident aortic stenosis cases), a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with very large variant count (1,119,377), and it reports a time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) plus a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92). Main limitation: the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariate adjustment (multiple cardiometabolic comorbidities and risk factors), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be isolated from the visible metadata.

Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005254 is also exact-match for aortic stenosis with a genome-wide method (PRS-CS), large variant count, and moderate HR (1.64) but lacks comparable discrimination metrics; PGS005255 and PGS005256 are closely related scores from the same publication family with similar design/covariates and weaker HR (~1.53) and their trait_reported are valve-function measurements rather than the disease label (though phenotyping_reported still states incident aortic stenosis). As a distant fourth runner-up from the visible list, PGS004911 is not a direct match (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), but is included only to satisfy the requirement to draw alternatives from the provided candidate list when direct-match runners-up are exhausted.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including two models explicitly mapped to EFO:arthritis (PGS001135 “Arthritis (nos)” and the “Other arthritis” models PGS004477/PGS004547). PGS001135 is the best-supported direct match because it has exact trait_efo alignment (arthritis) and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS R2=0.00291) plus full-model AUROC=0.674 with standard demographic/PC covariates, making its evidence package more interpretable than the ‘Other arthritis’ models that report only an OR without comparable discrimination metrics. However, the overall direct-match evidence remains sub-optimal because the PRS-only signal for PGS001135 is weak (very low PGS-only AUROC/R2) and several other candidates in the list target specific arthritis subtypes (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, osteoarthritis) rather than generic arthritis, limiting confidence that any single model is clearly optimal for the broad umbrella trait.

Direct-match candidates for asthma are present (many models with trait_efo=asthma). PGS002727 is best supported on visible evidence because it is explicitly phenotype-aligned to a clinically meaningful restricted endpoint ("Pediatric asthma"), reports a strong PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.57, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) alongside AUROC 0.66 and R2 0.04, and is described as a multiancestral pediatric-asthma PRS with very large validation (n=391,820). Main limitation: endpoint is pediatric-specific (not generic asthma), covariates are listed as Unknown, and the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC), so comparability across candidates remains imperfect.

Runners-up: (1) PGS001782 (Cell Genom global biobank PRS-CS-auto) is a direct asthma endpoint with genome-wide shrinkage and AUROC 0.659 plus covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 0.048844, but it is a framework-style global-biobank analysis and has only one performance record. (2) PGS001344 (UKB snpnet, doctor-diagnosed asthma) has strong endpoint fidelity and the highest full-model AUROC among the snpnet siblings shown (0.66621) with reported PGS-only AUROC/R2 fields present, but it comes from a pan-trait "813 traits" framework family (penalized sparse) which is penalized by the provided domain guidance. (3) PGS005134 (Cell Genom multi-ancestry meta-analysis PRS-CSx; EUR->EUR eval) is disease-focused and reports PRS R2=0.053582 (below the provided h2_liability ceiling 0.1515), but lacks AUROC/effect-size reporting in the visible record, limiting comparability. (4) PGS002061 (UKB portability LDpred2) is a direct asthma endpoint with a reasonable partial-r (0.1184) but lacks clearer PRS-only discrimination metrics and is from a portability framework, making it weaker than the above despite clean endpoint labeling.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo includes atopic eczema). The strongest endpoint-fidelity models for the generic target “atopic eczema” are those with phenotyping_reported = incident atopic dermatitis (PGS002755, PGS004587), whereas three candidates are therapy/context-specific (“paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis”: PGS003459, PGS003486, PGS004903) and one is restricted to a severity subtype (moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis: PGS001773). Between the two incident-atopic-dermatitis models, PGS002755 is preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants) and reports a moderate HR (high vs low PRS) of 1.249 (1.123–1.391) in a large European evaluation (n=337,910), providing more directly PRS-relevant evidence than PGS004587’s smaller HR (1.153, 1.037–1.282) with a sparse genome-wide-significant SNP set (23 variants). However, confidence is limited because none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R²; PGS001773’s very high full-model AUROC (0.93) is not treated as PRS-comparable and is further hard to reconcile with the trait heritability ceiling guidance, and several candidates have endpoint restrictions (paradoxical eczema; moderate-to-severe) that reduce direct applicability to generic atopic eczema risk.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (atrial fibrillation) by trait_reported/trait_efo and generally coherent phenotyping_reported. PGS005168 is best supported because it comes from a disease-focused AF meta-analysis publication (“Meta-analysis of genome-wide associations and polygenic risk prediction for atrial fibrillation in more than 180,000 cases.”), has endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (“Atrial fibrillation”), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), and reports strong validation discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) with basic covariates plus CHARGE-AF (noted in domain guidance as a risk-calculator packaging concern, but here it is included as a covariate rather than being framed as a fixed-horizon risk-wrapper endpoint). Main limitation: the reported metric is a full-model C-index (not explicitly PRS-only), and inclusion of CHARGE-AF in covariates reduces comparability to standalone PRS performance, lowering confidence.

Runners-up: (1) PGS005313 is also disease-focused with broad multi-cohort training and strong effect size (OR 1.82) and AUROC 0.78, but evaluation is MAE-only and the reported AUROC is not clearly PRS-only. (2) PGS002814 has very large disease-focused GWAS context and strong reported AUROC 0.74 and pseudo-R2 0.14 in East Asian evaluation, but it is EAS-only evaluation (less directly comparable if deployment ancestry is unspecified) and metrics are not explicitly PRS-only. (3) PGS000016 is a classic genome-wide LDpred AF score with explicit PRS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.029 (below the provided EUR h2 ceiling, thus plausible) and large validation, but it is older and its headline AUROC is full-model. (4) PGS000331 is disease-focused with incident AF endpoint and HR 1.62 plus C-index 0.751, but has smaller training size and lacks PRS-only metrics. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches to the target trait concept (atrial flutter appears explicitly in trait_reported/trait_efo for PGS001263, and in the combined AF+flutter endpoint for PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050). PGS001263 is the only model with an atrial-flutter-specific endpoint (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both 'Atrial flutter') and it reports PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.025, which are below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443) and therefore pass the sanity-check. However, confidence is limited because PGS001263 (and PGS001339) come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper ('across 813 traits'), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus more disease-focused scores; meanwhile the portability-framework scores (PGS001841/PGS002050) use genome-wide shrinkage/penalized regression with larger training n and many more variants but lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only partial-r), and their phenotype is broader (AF+flutter) rather than flutter-specific. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS002050 slightly ahead of PGS001841 due to marginally higher partial-r (0.1034 vs 0.1026) with otherwise identical endpoint/covariates/publication context; PGS001339 next because it has PRS-only AUROC/R2 but is time-to-event and not flutter-specific; the final slot repeats PGS001339 because no additional distinct runner-up exists.

Two direct-match candidates are present for autism spectrum disorder. PGS000327 is best supported because its phenotype alignment is coherent across fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all explicitly autism spectrum disorder) and it comes from an ASD-focused publication context, with supportive PRS signal evidence (OR per SD 1.33 with CI 1.30–1.36; full_model_r2 0.0245) under basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave). PGS002790 is a weaker direct match despite having trait_reported/trait_efo as ASD, because phenotyping_reported is explicitly different ('Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)'), making endpoint fidelity unclear; its reported metric is also smaller (partial R² ~0.00546) and it lacks effect-size reporting. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because neither model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS-only AUC/R²), and the best model’s reported R² appears to be a full-model metric rather than an explicitly PRS-only metric, limiting comparability and certainty.

All 20 visible candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma). The strongest support in the visible evidence comes from the coherent Cancer PRSweb (Am J Hum Genet, 2020-12-15) cluster with consistent EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL and basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), allowing within-family comparison using the reported full-model AUROC and effect sizes (noting domain guidance that full-model AUROC is not a PRS-only metric). Within that cluster, PGS000452 (GWAS Hits, 28 variants) has the highest reported full-model AUROC (0.632; 0.616–0.647, tied) and the strongest per-SD OR (1.663; 1.57–1.761) plus strong top-1% vs rest OR (3.61), making it the best-supported direct-match choice from the available metadata. Runners-up are the closest near-clones with essentially identical AUROC and effect-size support: PGS000454 (P+T, 27 variants; AUROC 0.632; OR 1.661; top-1% OR 3.79), then PGS000456 (GWAS Hits, 30 variants; AUROC 0.63; OR 1.633; top-1% OR 3.95), then PGS000458 (P+T, 23 variants; AUROC 0.628; OR 1.634; top-1% OR 4.03), then PGS000447 (P+T, 72 variants; AUROC 0.591; OR 1.398). Main limitation: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R2, so discrimination comparisons rely on full-model AUROC and ORs under similar covariates; additionally, newer 2023 Nat Commun models (PGS003416/PGS003417, including an MTAG variant) have multi-cohort development but lack AUROC/R2 in the visible record and have phenotyping_reported as broader 'Keratinocyte cancers', which reduces certainty about outperforming the well-characterized PRSweb cluster. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. PGS001824 is the best-supported direct match because it targets the exact EFO term (bilirubin metabolism disease) with a specific endpoint (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”) and provides a PRS-comparable performance metric (partial correlation 0.0716 with CI) under basic covariates; it also comes from the same UKB-based portability study as a near-clone comparator, making endpoint fidelity clear. PGS002032 is the closest runner-up: same endpoint, same study, same reported partial-r, but with a more genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) and far higher variant count; however, the visible evidence does not show any performance separation between the two siblings, so preference is uncertain. PGS000924 is a broader composite endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”) and is explicitly time-to-event from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (a domain-knowledge warning signal), despite reporting high AUROC/full-model metrics; those metrics are less comparable and the framework/time-to-event context lowers confidence. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the top two direct-match candidates are effectively indistinguishable on the only comparable metric shown (partial-r), and the third candidate’s strong-looking AUROC comes from a framework/time-to-event setting that domain guidance cautions against over-weighting. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present (3 total) and all come from the same publication, method family (SDPR), training cohort context (PGC), and EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, so they are broadly comparable as bipolar-disorder PRSs. However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly mismatched across all three because their `phenotyping_reported` fields are non-diagnostic behavioral/cognitive measures (e.g., cognitive function; DSM5 depression; sluggish cognitive tempo) rather than a bipolar disorder case-control/diagnosis endpoint, which is the primary alignment signal per the provided domain guidance. Performance evidence is also limited to small partial R² values from full-model context (no PGS-only AUC/R²; no effect sizes), making it hard to confidently distinguish models.

Given the target is broad ‘bipolar disorder’, PGS002786 is selected as best because it is the only candidate whose `trait_reported` and `trait_efo` exactly match the umbrella target concept (bipolar disorder), whereas PGS002787 and PGS002788 are subtype-specific (bipolar I / bipolar II). Among runners-up, PGS002788 is next by slightly higher reported partial R² than the other subtype score, followed by PGS002787. Overall confidence remains low because the key limitation (phenotype/endpoint mismatch) applies to all candidates and the available performance metrics are not clearly PRS-only/comparable.

Direct-match candidates are present (3 total) but none is a clearly strong, disease-focused PRS for the broad target “blood coagulation disease”; all are UK Biobank framework/portability-derived endpoints with limited or non-comparable performance reporting, so the direct-match choice is sub-optimal.

Best pick: PGS001033 is the only candidate whose mapped trait_efo exactly matches the target (“blood coagulation disease”) and it provides the most explicit PRS-comparable discrimination evidence (PGS-only AUROC 0.634 and PGS-only R² 0.0578; basic covariates only). However, its endpoint is “Other coagulation defects (time-to-event)” (TTE), it is extremely sparse (1 variant), and it comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk—together lowering confidence.

Runners-up: PGS002034 and PGS001826 target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency phenotype (trait_efo: congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency), so phenotype alignment to the broad target is weaker than PGS001033. Between them, PGS002034 is structurally stronger (LDpred2 with 32,552 variants vs penalized regression with 45 variants) while their reported partial correlations are essentially identical (~0.0563 vs ~0.0562) and neither reports AUROC/R², making them hard to separate beyond method/variant-count signals. PGS001826 is therefore ranked behind PGS002034. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are abundant for the target EFO (breast carcinoma). Among the visible list, PGS004153 is best supported as a direct breast cancer PRS because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: “Breast cancer”), no added covariates (covariates=0, reducing risk of covariate-driven AUROC inflation), and it comes from a disease-focused multi-method evaluation within the same endpoint family with the strongest reported discrimination/variance among that cluster (full_model_auc≈0.6625; R²≈0.0764; OR≈1.83). The top runners-up are the closest competitors from the same coherent study family/endpoints with similarly clean covariates and very similar performance (PGS004040 and PGS004025 have nearly identical AUROC/R²/OR; PGS004083 and PGS004069 are slightly lower but still strong). Confidence is Moderate because the evidence relies on full-model AUROC/R² (not explicitly labeled as PGS-only), and several near-tied models in the same family make the ‘best’ choice sensitive to small, potentially non-meaningful metric differences.

All 10 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = celiac disease), so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS000316 is best supported overall because it has an endpoint-faithful phenotype (“Coeliac disease”), is disease-focused (clinical-care pilot study rather than a pan-trait/portability framework), and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.879 with CI) with very large validation sample size (n=379,767), providing comparatively rich and coherent evidence among the direct-match set. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as “Unknown,” and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this keeps confidence at Moderate. Runners-up were ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000040 (disease-focused celiac prediction study; very high reported AUROC 0.9 but also full-model and smaller validation), PGS001301 (explicit PGS-only and full-model metrics reported, but from a pan-trait UKB framework and phenotype is a composite “Malabsorption/coeliac disease”), then the UKB portability-framework celiac scores with the strongest available PRS-comparable metric (partial-r), led by PGS002067 (highest partial-r among those). | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 visible candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported consistently cervical cancer, mostly incident cervical cancer). Best-supported pick is PGS003428 because it comes from a cervical-phenotype-focused GWAS meta-analysis paper and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred; 2,894,555 variants), which is structurally favored over sparse/GWAS-hit scores when endpoint fidelity is comparable; it also reports a moderate per-SD HR (1.33). Main limitation: the only reported discrimination is a full-model C-index (0.613) with covariates (age, smoking) and no PGS-only AUROC/R², so performance comparability across candidates is limited and confidence cannot be high. Runners-up: PGS000073 and PGS000784 have strong endpoint fidelity (incident cervical cancer) and large EUR evaluation (n=211,795) with similar reported full-model AUROC (~0.745) and modest HR (~1.21–1.22), but they are GWAS-hit style (10 variants) and come from cross-/pan-cancer risk-factor integration contexts, making full-model AUROC less informative for PRS-only quality. PGS005165 is a direct cervical cancer score in an East Asian (EAS) context (GWAS/EVAL EAS) with modest HR (~1.2) but lower reported C-index (0.566) and ancestry specificity. PGS003389 (lassosum; 2,814 variants) has weaker reported discrimination (AUROC 0.563) and very low R² (0.00158). The remaining candidate PGS001299 is deprioritized because it is from a pan-trait UKB framework (snpnet; sparse 24 variants) with weak PGS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.55; PGS R² ~0.0026), which domain guidance flags as less reliable than disease-focused models when available.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but the evidence quality is mixed. PGS004546 (K80 cholelithiasis) is preferred because it is an endpoint-faithful ICD10 K80 model and, within its same-publication sibling pair (Commun Biol 2024; same cohorts, variant count, and EUR-only eval), it reports the stronger per-SD effect size (OR=1.2986 vs 1.2194 for PGS004476), which is the main available discriminative signal given missing PRS-comparable AUC/R2 for these 2024 models and unknown covariates. Runners-up: PGS004476 is the closest sibling with slightly weaker OR; PGS005150 is also endpoint-faithful and uses a modern cross-ancestry PRS-CSx design with EAS evaluation (useful if East Asian deployment is intended) but provides only a beta effect size and lacks AUC/R2; PGS002072 and PGS001861 are direct-match composite endpoints (cholelithiasis and cholecystitis) from a portability framework and only report partial-r (0.098 and 0.0948), offering limited comparability. PGS001174 reports explicit PRS-only metrics but is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework with a time-to-event endpoint, which domain guidance flags as less reliable for external performance despite better-formatted metrics; this creates residual uncertainty, keeping confidence at Moderate rather than High.

All 22 visible candidates are direct EFO matches to chronic kidney disease, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and how interpretable their reported performance is as PRS-specific. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD-focused (Nat Med: "Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries"), uses a clear clinical endpoint (CKD stage 3+ / eGFR <45), has large development (n=279,819), multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a meaningful per-SD effect size (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65). Its reported AUROC (0.78) is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates, so it is discounted per the provided domain guidance; nonetheless, the endpoint alignment + disease-focused study context + effect size make it the strongest overall direct-match package in the visible list.

Runners-up: (1) PGS005090 has very strong reported discrimination (AUROC=0.9; R²=0.1; OR=1.41) and a CKD stage 3+ framing, but it is AFR-only (GWAS/EVAL AFR) and the very high metrics are not PRS-only, making general direct-match selection less certain without a specified deployment ancestry. (2) PGS005113 is CKDGen-trained with a strong OR=1.35 and clean/basic covariates, but lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R² and has mixed/unclear evaluation ancestry details. (3) PGS004889 targets incident CKD without diabetes and reports HR=1.3 with multi-ancestry evaluation, but the endpoint is restricted (incident, non-diabetic) and the reported C-index is full-model with a clinical risk score component, reducing PRS comparability. (4) PGS002757 is an exact CKD label with OR=1.15 (weaker effect size) and no other performance metrics, so it ranks below the stronger effect-size and/or more CKD-focused alternatives.

Main limitation: across the pool, PRS-only metrics are largely absent and several high AUROC/C-index values are full-model with substantial clinical covariates, so confidence is limited by metric comparability rather than lack of direct-match candidates.

All 10 visible candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target COPD concept via trait_efo=chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (or closely adjacent emphysema). The strongest-supported direct-match choice from the visible evidence is PGS001783 because it is an exact COPD endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both COPD) and, compared to the other exact-COPD candidates, it provides a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) plus a reported AUROC (0.74) in EUR evaluation; its PRS-comparable R2 is also consistent with the provided COPD heritability ceiling guidance (h2_liability≈0.0388), supporting metric plausibility. Runners-up: PGS001788 is the closest competitor (same publication family, exact COPD endpoint, very large EUR validation n=337,168 but lower covariates-regressed-out R2=0.0163). Among the UKB snpnet COPD variants, PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334 are all endpoint-faithful (COPD EFO; COPD phenotyping variants) with explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 reported, but they come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (a known generalization risk per domain knowledge) and show weak PGS-only discrimination (AUROC ~0.54; R2 ~0.002–0.003), making them less supported than the multi-biobank PRS-CS-auto COPD models. ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034), both mapped to the target EFO term and sharing the same reported/phenotyped endpoint (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”), same publication family (UKB portability framework), similar EUR-focused development/evaluation ancestry, identical covariate set (basic demographics + PCs), and essentially identical reported partial correlation (0.0563 vs 0.0562 with overlapping CIs). With no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and no effect sizes reported for either, performance evidence is limited and does not clearly separate them. Given the domain guidance that, when PRS-only AUC is absent across candidates, methodological properties and structural signals become the main differentiators, PGS002034 is weakly preferred because it uses LDpred2 (genome-wide shrinkage) with many more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is generally a stronger structural configuration than a very sparse penalized regression score when endpoints and covariates are otherwise the same. Confidence remains low because both models come from the same portability framework study and the observed performance metric is minimal and nearly identical, leaving no decisive empirical advantage.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all state corneal dystrophy) and come from the same UK Biobank portability framework paper with the same training cohort (UKB), training size (n=391,124), covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs), and validation sample size (n=19,321), so endpoint fidelity and study context do not differentiate them. The main differentiators available are (i) the selected European validation partial correlation and (ii) structural properties: PGS002042 (LDpred2; 59,944 variants) shows higher partial-r (0.0471 vs 0.0384) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with far more variants than PGS001835 (penalized regression; 38 variants), which is supportive under the provided domain guidance when endpoints are otherwise identical. Direct-match candidates for the target trait (dementia) are present, including multiple models with trait_efo='dementia' and/or phenotyping_reported explicitly referencing incident all-cause dementia. Key limitation: its reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 shown), and the development/validation sample sizes are relatively small (n≈2,039/2,032), so the strength of the PRS-alone contribution is not fully resolvable from the visible metadata.

Runners-up were ranked by remaining direct-match support emphasizing phenotype alignment and available PRS-comparable metrics: (1) PGS000823 has excellent endpoint fidelity ('Incident all-cause dementia') and a relatively strong reported HR contrast (top vs bottom third HR=1.36) in a disease-focused cohort context, but lacks explicit PRS-only metrics. Confidence is not High because (i) none of these report PRS-only AUROC/R² explicitly (the reported R² may be full-model or otherwise not clearly PRS-only), (ii) several near-clone models are extremely close in support, and (iii) some other direct-match entries have non-comparable or endpoint-mismatched phenotyping (e.g., antidepressant side-effect phenotype; brain imaging phenotype) or potentially non-comparable metric reporting, limiting clean cross-study discrimination. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to diverticular disease (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align to diverticular disease/K57/diverticulitis). PGS000997 is best supported because it provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.591 and PGS-only R2=0.01777) with basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a clear diverticular disease endpoint (time-to-event). Main limitation: it comes from a known pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores externally; additionally, the endpoint is time-to-event rather than a generic case-control disease status, which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty for a generic ‘diverticular disease’ target.

Runners-up: PGS004614 is disease-focused (Cell Genom diverticular disease study) with an aligned endpoint and genome-wide shrinkage method (SBayesR) and reports a high full-model AUROC (0.76), but lacks PRS-only metrics and uses family history as a covariate, making the AUROC less comparable to standalone PRS performance. PGS004544 and PGS004474 (same Commun Biol study family; K57 endpoint) provide moderate per-SD ORs (~1.32) but no AUC/R2 and have unknown covariates, limiting comparability; PGS004544 is ranked slightly above PGS004474 due to the marginally higher OR. PGS000996 is also a pan-trait UKB snpnet score with weaker PRS-only metrics (PGS-only R2=0.00372; AUROC=0.552) and a broader combined phenotype (diverticular disease/diverticulitis), so it ranks last among direct matches.

All 4 candidates are direct-match to the target disease family (juvenile idiopathic arthritis), come from the same disease-focused publication (Ann Rheum Dis: “Genomic risk scores for juvenile idiopathic arthritis and its subtypes.”), use the same method (SparSNP), and have similar basic covariates (sex, genetic PCs 1–10) with EUR-only development/evaluation—so endpoint fidelity and study archetype are broadly consistent across the set.

Its reported validation AUROC (full-model AUROC 0.738 with CI 0.705–0.77) and per-SD OR (2.085) provide supportive discrimination evidence under comparable covariates.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (kidney cancer) via trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (kidney cancer / renal carcinoma / renal cell carcinoma; several explicitly use incident kidney cancer). PGS004908 is best supported because it is kidney-cancer-specific, reports the strongest visible discrimination among candidates (full-model AUROC 0.74 with CI 0.72–0.75) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.5, CI 1.43–1.58), with covariates that are standard epidemiologic/demographic (age, sex, PCs, BMI, smoking, hypertension) rather than obvious clinical leakage, and it is backed by a large disease-focused GWAS effort (multi-ancestry GWAS; EUR evaluation). Main limitation: across the pool, PRS-only (covariate-free) AUC/R2 is not reported, so comparisons rely on full-model AUROC and per-SD OR/HR, which are not perfectly comparable across differing covariate sets and study designs; this keeps confidence at Moderate.

Runner-up ordering: PGS000076 and PGS000787 are endpoint-faithful (incident kidney cancer / renal cell carcinoma as dominant subtype) and show similar full-model AUROC (~0.722) plus HR ~1.15–1.16 with large validation (n~391k), but they come from cross-/pan-cancer risk-factor-integrated contexts and do not exceed PGS004908’s effect-size evidence. PGS000722 is also incident kidney cancer with a larger validation (n~401k) but has weaker full-model AUROC (0.567). Direct-match candidates for the target trait (kidney failure) are present, including PGS004562 and PGS004492 (both trait_efo=kidney failure; phenotyping_reported=N18 chronic renal failure) and PGS000708 (trait_reported=Kidney failure but phenotyping_reported specifies diabetic kidney failure). All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target (knee osteoarthritis) via trait_efo=osteoarthritis, knee and consistent trait/phenotyping labels (gonarthrosis/knee OA). PGS002767 is preferred because it has strong PRS-discrimination evidence via an explicit per-SD effect size (OR=1.35, 95% CI 1.3–1.4) on a directly aligned knee OA endpoint with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/technical), and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (~1.05M), which is structurally favorable for a polygenic disease. However, confidence is not high because several other direct-match models have limited or non-PRS-comparable performance reporting (e.g., only full-model AUROC or only OR/HR without clear PRS-only metrics), making cross-model comparison uncertain; additionally, PGS002729 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.66) with BMI included (not PRS-only), and the 2024 Commun Biol siblings (PGS004479/PGS004549) have unknown covariates and only OR point estimates. Runner-up ordering reflects remaining direct-match support: PGS002729 (disease-focused knee/hip OA PRS paper with clinical OA endpoint and reported AUROC, albeit full-model), then PGS004549 and PGS004479 (same endpoint family, genome-wide models with moderate ORs but unknown covariates), then PGS004883 (incident knee OA with C-index=0.6 and HR=1.37 but unusual training cohort listing and small samples_training), while PGS001192 is deprioritized despite having PRS-only metrics because it is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (known weaker external generalization) and shows weak PRS-only signal (AUROC~0.557; R2~0.0068).

All 5 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo = late-onset Alzheimer's disease). The strongest visible PRS-comparable evidence comes from the Neurology study pair PGS000053/PGS000054: both use the same endpoint family (familial late-onset AD), same simple covariates (age, sex), same sparse GWAS-hits construction (21 variants), and report per-SD odds ratios. Between them, PGS000054 has the stronger reported effect size (OR 1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) than PGS000053 (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.21–1.37), which is supportive of better discrimination per the provided domain guidance; the main limitation is that PGS000054 is evaluated in AMR (Hispanic/Latin American) only, while the target deployment ancestry is unspecified and most other candidates are EUR-evaluated.

Runners-up ranking: (1) PGS000053 remains strong due to the same clean endpoint/covariate design and EUR evaluation, but has a weaker OR. (2) PGS000334 has a direct LOAD endpoint and reports an R²=0.191, but this is a C+T score with unknown covariates and the domain guidance flags very high R² from thresholding pipelines as potentially non-comparable/suspect; GWAS ancestry is also mixed/NR. (3) PGS004918 reports a full-model AUROC=0.731 but provides no PGS-only metric and has small dev/eval samples (n=439 training; n=136 validation) plus a pathway-restricted 8-SNP design, so the AUROC is hard to interpret for standalone PRS ranking. (4) PGS002289 is labeled LOAD but its phenotyping_reported is a cognition-by-age interaction outcome rather than AD diagnosis, making endpoint fidelity weaker for a disease-risk PRS despite very large validation size.

Direct-match candidates are abundant (multiple PGS explicitly for lung cancer / lung carcinoma / malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung). PGS000078 is best supported overall because it is a direct lung cancer PRS with large European evaluation (n=392,539), reports effect size (HR=1.16, 95% CI 1.11–1.22) and discrimination metrics (AUROC=0.846; C-index=0.849), and has coherent endpoint wording (incident lung cancer). However, the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with extensive covariates (including family history, PM2.5, detailed smoking terms and interactions), and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the apparent performance advantage may be substantially covariate-driven; this prevents a high-confidence, high-quality designation. Runners-up: PGS000789 is essentially the same lung cancer score/endpoint/covariate set (109 variants derived from PGS000078) with similar metrics (AUROC=0.846; HR=1.17), making it a near-tie but less primary than the original. PGS004860 has very high reported AUROC (0.893) and reports R2=0.49, but these are full-model metrics with covariates and come from a specific French-Canadian case-control cohort (n=24,012), so comparability/transportability is less clear from the visible metadata. PGS000740 is direct but targets early-onset lung cancer (<50 years), an endpoint restriction relative to generic lung cancer. PGS000721 is a direct lung cancer GWAS-hits score with modestly lower full-model AUROC (0.738) and smaller validation (n=1,202), but has clean phenotype alignment and multi-cohort development context. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple SLE and lupus erythematosus models), but the pool has important endpoint and metric comparability limitations (many report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates; one uses phenotype-risk-score covariate packaging; several target restricted sub-phenotypes like early-onset or renal/nephritis manifestations), so no single option is unambiguously best.

PGS000754 is preferred because it has strong phenotype alignment to the target disease concept (systemic lupus erythematosus), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (lassosum) with very large variant count (293,684) consistent with capturing polygenic signal, and has reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.65) in a sizable validation (n=7,733) with evaluation including European ancestry. Main limitation: the reported AUROC is full-model (not explicitly PRS-only) and covariates are unknown, so the PRS contribution cannot be isolated from the visible evidence.

Runners-up: PGS000328 and PGS000196 are direct SLE diagnosis-oriented models with higher reported full-model AUROC (0.83 and 0.79 respectively) but are based on small GWAS-hit SNP sets and have endpoint restrictions (PGS000328 is early-onset SLE; PGS000196 is SLE diagnosis in an arthritis outpatient context), with unknown covariates and no PRS-only metrics. PGS004917 is a direct SLE model with supportive effect size evidence (OR 2.01 reported) and AUROC 0.696, but appears tied to a smoking-interaction study context and has unknown covariates, reducing comparability. PGS003960 reports very high full-model AUROC (0.89) for SLE, but explicitly includes a phenotype risk score covariate (non-genetic packaging/leakage), making the AUROC non-comparable for standalone PRS ranking despite strong apparent discrimination.

Direct-match candidates are present for the target trait (lymphoid leukemia), including models explicitly mapped to the lymphoid leukemia EFO (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305) and closely aligned subtype models (multiple chronic lymphocytic leukemia scores). PGS000077 is the best-supported direct match because its phenotyping_reported is a direct endpoint (“Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia”), it is explicitly mapped to lymphoid leukemia, it uses only basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), and it reports supportive effect-size evidence (HR 1.45) with large European evaluation (n=391,338). However, confidence is not High because most candidates report only full-model discrimination (not PRS-only metrics), making AUROC/C-index comparisons non-comparable across differing model/covariate contexts; additionally, PGS000788 shows stronger full-model metrics and HR but is explicitly a re-weighted derivative of PGS000077 (“inverse variant weights”), and several CLL-focused models show strong apparent discrimination but are subtype-/population-restricted (e.g., family-history-enriched PGS000874) or have missing/unclear covariate/performance details (e.g., PGS003453). Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000788 (same endpoint, stronger HR/full-model metrics but derivative reweighting), PGS000645 (exact lymphoid leukemia label/EFO but very sparse 6-variant P+T and weaker AUROC), PGS002305 (mapped to lymphoid leukemia with modest AUROC and small validation n=265), and PGS003453 (CLL subtype with strong OR but lacks reported AUROC and has unknown covariates, so endpoint/performance comparability is limited).

PGS004606 is best supported overall because it has tight phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Age-related macular degeneration), comes from a disease-focused AMD genetics study (Nat Genet 2024), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.0M variants), and provides supportive performance/effect evidence (full-model AUROC 0.71 with basic covariates; OR per SD 1.76). Main limitation: the reported AUROC appears to be full-model (no PGS-only AUROC/R² shown), so PRS-only discrimination cannot be directly compared across candidates. PGS004952 reports a very high AUROC but it is likely a full-model metric and is internally inconsistent in the record (classification_metrics AUROC listed as 84.2 vs performance_metrics.full_model_auc 0.842) plus it targets late AMD specifically with small validation (n=1,232), so it is discounted despite endpoint relevance. PGS001013 has explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.553; PGS R² ~0.006) but is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (snpnet; 53 variants) with weak PRS-only performance, making it less preferred than disease-focused AMD scores. PGS002269 is AMD-labeled but its phenotyping_reported is a retinal layer thickness biomarker proxy rather than a direct AMD diagnosis endpoint, reducing endpoint fidelity for generic macular degeneration risk despite multi-cohort context.

Direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma / phenotyping_reported melanoma endpoints). The overall outcome is still DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the visible performance evidence is limited and not directly comparable across all models (no PGS-only AUROC/R² for most; PGS001250 reports full-model AUROC and incremental AUROC but domain guidance cautions against relying on full-model AUROC), and two 2024 models (PGS004493/PGS004563) report only per-SD ORs (~1.23–1.28, i.e., modest) with unknown covariates, leaving uncertainty about standalone PRS discrimination and comparability.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (uterine cancer) are present, including two exact EFO matches to uterine cancer (PGS000541, PGS000542) and additional near-synonymous uterine/corpus uteri/endometrial carcinoma models. PGS000541 is best supported because it has exact phenotype alignment (trait_efo=uterine cancer; phenotyping_reported=Malignant neoplasm of uterus), clean/basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs), and provides interpretable effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.311) plus AUROC with CI in European evaluation. PGS000542 is a very close sibling (same endpoint/covariates/validation) but has slightly weaker reported AUROC and OR per SD, so it ranks second. Among remaining direct matches, PGS001795 (uterine cancer) is endpoint-aligned and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count, but it comes from a global biobank framework context and shows very small PRS-comparable R2 (0.001948), limiting confidence. PGS003740 (Corpus Uteri) is anatomically aligned but has small validation (n=372) and sparse metrics. PGS000786 (endometrial cancer; dominant uterine subtype per provided domain knowledge) is a strong semantic match but is not an exact uterine-cancer label and reports only full-model metrics (no PGS-only AUROC), so it is ranked behind the uterus-labeled models. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (vitiligo) by trait_reported/trait_efo. PGS000738 is preferred because its phenotyping_reported is most consistent with a direct vitiligo disease endpoint (no explicit therapy-induced or proxy framing), whereas PGS000760’s phenotyping_reported is explicitly treatment/context-specific (anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients), creating endpoint-fidelity concerns despite the vitiligo label. PGS001536 is also a direct vitiligo endpoint but is a time-to-event UK Biobank pan-trait framework score (PLoS Genet ‘across 813 traits’), which domain guidance flags as typically less reliable externally than disease-focused scores; its reported AUROC/R2 are supportive but do not fully offset the framework penalty. Overall confidence is Moderate because PGS000738 has missing/limited PRS-comparable performance reporting (no AUC/R2; only a pseudo R² and a beta) and has an anomalous phenotyping_reported field (‘Red hair’) that introduces residual ambiguity, preventing a clearly high-quality selection. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.
